highlights.title: Apple will limit Mac disk access as AI agents ‘substantially’ increase risk
highlights.summary: Apple will add new limits for "full disk access" on Mac in response to risks posed by AI agents, as reported earlier by TechCrunch. In an update on Friday, Apple says it's rolling out new controls to "ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only…
body: Mac apps will soon need ‘very explicit user action’ to gain full disk access, according to Apple.

The change comes just weeks after Inc ’s Jason Aten found that Meta’s Muse AI somehow knew the contents of his messages, despite not giving the chatbot explicit permission to access them on his iPhone or Mac. Meta spokesperson Andy Stone pushed back on this report, saying access to Messages is “entirely opt-in.” Stone added that you have to “enable both Full Disk Access and the Messages connector for Muse to be able to read your Messages content.”

Some developers are using Full Disk Access in ways that could put users at risk, exposing everything on their systems—including files, mail, messages, and even browsing history—without users’ full knowledge and understanding… As AI agents become increasingly capable and autonomous, the risks associated with this level of access will grow substantially.

highlights.summary: James Wade and Nathan Aspinall put in statement performances that will have made their semi-final opponents take note ahead of a mouthwatering Saturday night line-up at the World Grand Prix.
body: Aspinall threatened to set a new tournament record average when storming to a 3-0 win over Ryan Joyce, his 105.15 mark ultimately landing as the fourth-highest in history and the best-ever in a quarter-final.
Wade, meanwhile, dropped only one leg as he, in his words, "bashed up" world No 2 Gian van Veen in a match that lasted little more than 20 minutes.
"That really was a performance to remember from Wade," Sky Sports ' Wayne Mardle said. "From start to finish, he was absolutely devastating. World Class."
Three-time world champion John Part concurred with that assesment, saying: "James is not just looking like a great dart thrower to me, he's looking like a winner.

highlights.title: Capcom Announces Plans to Transform the RE Engine Into an AI-Generation Game Engine — ‘Our Goal Is a Future Where We Create Games Together With AI’
highlights.summary: Resident Evil and Street Fighter developer Capcom revealed some big changes coming to its RE Engine, which they plan to incrementally improve and transform into an "AI-generation game engine." On October 2, Capcom held its own tech conference, called ‘Capcom Open Conference RE: 2026.’ One of the…
body: As reported by Japanese news outlet GameBiz, Ishida mentioned three major issues that Capcom is currently experiencing when it comes to game development: First, games are now so massive that simple processes have become extremely time-consuming; increased numbers of staff mean an engine is needed that’s easy for everyone to use; and finally, “successfully integrating AI technology into development workflows has become an essential condition for streamlining future development.”

GameBiz’s report confirmed that REX was created to help solve these problems by improving the efficiency of game development, game performance, tools, quality assurance, etc. Capcom felt that, rather than creating a brand-new engine from scratch, gradually adding these improvements over time is the best way to help evolve the RE Engine to the next generation.

We won’t get into the weeds of all the specific improvements included in the REX program, but Capcom is making at least some of them open-source for the purpose of training AI. Most interestingly, AI plays into Capcom’s larger, long-term goal of turning the RE Engine into an “AI-generation game engine” using its REX improvements.

highlights.title: Supercell, Rovio, Playdemic, First Touch, Sybo and more back SpecialEffect’s One Special Day
highlights.summary: Many major mobile game makers are giving a percentage of their UK revenue to disability charity Special Effect today, Friday October 2. Partners taking part in the One Special Day promotion include Supercell, Rovio, Sybo, Playdemic, Fingersoft, Supersolid, Hyper Luminal Games, New Star Games…
body: A slice of player spend from games including Clash of Clans, Brawl Stars, Clash Royale, Angry Birds 2, Golf Clash, Subway Surfers, Dream League Soccer, 8 Ball Pool and more will be donated to Special Effect for today only. A full list of participating games is available via the One Special Day site.

Special Effect provides assessments and customised technology loans to help physically disabled people play games, and takes what it learns back to hardware and software developers to help make their products more accessible. Thousands of disabled people ask for the charity’s help every year.

“We’ve been proud to partner with Special Effect across our games for nearly a decade, and that relationship has grown far beyond One Special Day,” said Supercell’s Deborah Mensah-Bonsu. “From cycling in Helsinki and joining One Special Walk in London, to learning from their incredible work as we think more deeply about inclusive design, we’re continually inspired by their tenacity, generosity and tremendous heart, and by how they show the games industry can genuinely change lives for the better.”

highlights.title: Spoiler alert! Is social media ruining big gig surprises?
highlights.summary: Big moments from headline acts are shared online long before many fans see their favourite artists.
body: Months before you have a chance to see your favourite artist, chances are you already know some of the big moments they have planned.
You'll also probably know the set list, the stage design, and - if you've really been paying attention - where to stand to get the best view.
When it comes to films and TV series, spoilers tend to be guarded against with warnings.
But for many major gigs, there's no escaping a stream of fan videos from the shows if you're online, whether you like it or not.

highlights.title: Apple changes full-disk access permissions to curb abuse from AI agents
highlights.summary: Apple says it is changing its macOS privacy settings to stop third-party app developers from misusing them to access message histories. Friday's announcement comes two weeks after tech columnist Jason Aten said that Meta’s new general-purpose AI agent Muse sent him an unsolicited notification…
body: Meta CTO David Singleton joined the fray with a rebuttal that appeared solid. For Muse to access Apple Messages, a user must manually give it two privileges. One is full-disk access, a macOS system-level permission. The other is to enable a Messages connector setting in Muse.

“The Messages integration in the Muse Mac app is opt in,” Singleton said. “Your Muse can only read Messages content if macOS system-level Full Disk Access is granted and the Messages connector is enabled.”
Singleton’s implication was clear. Muse could have read Aten’s Messages communications only if he had enabled both settings, and if so, the columnist had only himself—and certainly not Meta—to blame.

Some developers are using Full Disk Access in ways that could put users at risk, exposing everything on their systems—including files, mail, messages, and even browsing history—without users’ full knowledge and understanding. For communication apps, this can also compromise the privacy of the people users are communicating with.
points: Apple says it is changing its macOS privacy settings to stop third-party app developers from misusing them to access message histories.
For Muse to access Apple Messages, a user must manually give it two privileges.

“The Messages integration in the Muse Mac app is opt in,” Singleton said.

highlights.title: Computational tools for society’s most complex challenges
highlights.summary: Associate Professor Cathy Wu uses reinforcement learning to help map out improvements to transportation and other multifaceted systems.
body: As far back as she can remember, Cathy Wu ’12, MNG ’13 wanted to find ways to solve problems to improve people’s lives. Her parents were Taiwanese immigrants, and her father had a long commute to his job, which took him away from the family. On a tight budget, the rest of the family often stayed home on a street that was too busy for playing outdoors. Wu and her siblings ended up playing a lot of computer games.

Wu says her desire to make the world a better place, her dad’s daily battle against traffic, and the games she played, like “SimCity,” were the seeds of her motivation to design safe, efficient transportation systems.

Wu is an associate professor in the MIT Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering (CEE) and the Institute for Data, Systems, and Society (IDSS), and a principal investigator in the Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems. Her research focuses on using machine learning and reinforcement learning (RL) to advance reliable strategies for improving a range of complex systems, including transportation.

highlights.title: Brown scores twice as Northen Ireland cruise to win over Ukraine
highlights.summary: Ciaron Brown's first international goals came as a pair to help a young Northern Ireland side stun Ukraine 3-0 and go clear at the top of Nations League Group B2.
body: Brown, the only player in Michael O'Neill's starting line-up over the age of 24, scrambled in early on before Isaac Price doubled the lead in the 22nd minute at the Stadion Antona Malatinskeho in Trnava, Slovakia.

Brown's second then came in bizarre fashion just after the hour - the 28-year-old Oxford defender went up to flick on Pierce Charles' free-kick from inside the Northern Ireland half and Ukraine goalkeeper Dmytro Riznyk let the bouncing ball through his legs.

On paper this was the hardest game in the group, away to a side ranked 37 places above Northern Ireland, but they brushed Ukraine aside to move on to seven points from their opening three games since returning to their second tier, still yet to concede going into Monday's game with Georgia in Belfast.

This was the first competitive meeting with Ukraine since Northern Ireland's famous 2-0 win at Euro 2016, and they delivered a performance which will have fans believing a major tournament beckons for this new generation.

highlights.title: Quentin Tarantino's First Movie Sequel Officially Arrives Next Month
highlights.summary: Seven years after the fact, Quentin Tarantino's period action-drama Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood is getting an official sequel, just not one directed by Tarantino himself.
body: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth — previously known simply as The Adventures of Cliff Booth — will make its Netflix debut on Dec. 23, but audiences will have a chance to see it in theaters much sooner.

Fincher and Tarantino fans will get an early look at the film in November. Netflix has an exclusive two-week run in IMAX theaters starting Nov. 25. So if you want to see what a Fincher-led sequel to Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood looks like on the biggest screen, you have a limited window.

Pitt will reprise his Best Supporting Actor Academy Award-winning role as Cliff Booth in the film. While the original film was set in 1969, the sequel will take place in 1977 in "a very different Hollywood," Netflix says. The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth also stars Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, Peter Weller, Matt Groove, JB Tadena, Corey Fogelmanis, and Karren Karagulian. Fincher directed from a script written by Tarantino, the latter of which has not revealed his 10th and final film-directing project.

highlights.title: Video Games Europe hits back at EU watchdog targeting King, Supercell, Mojang and more over IAP practices
highlights.summary: The EU’s Consumer Protection Cooperation Network has launched coordinated enforcement actions against games companies including King, Supercell, Mojang, Riot Games, Activision Blizzard and Ubisoft, over how they sell and handle in-game virtual currencies.
body: The CPC Network brings together national consumer protection authorities from across the EU and EEA and is coordinated by the European Commission. In a joint statement published September 30, it said it had found that “a high number of video game companies” had made no substantive changes to their practices since it published non-binding “Key Principles” on in-game currencies in March 2025, despite extensive subsequent talks with industry bodies.

It said the coordinated actions are particularly focused on compliance around variable reward systems such as loot boxes, “dark patterns” and other “harmful influencing techniques”, and practices that directly exhort children to spend money, which it says EU law already prohibits.
Video Games Europe and the European Game Developers Federation pushed back on the CPC Network’s actions in a statement also published on September 30.

highlights.title: “Good Heavens”: Kathleen Turner Reacts to Michael Douglas’ Bombshell About Their Secret Romance During ‘Romancing the Stone’
highlights.summary: The two-time Oscar nominee revealed via a new excerpt from his 'One Helluva Ride' memoir that they had an affair during production on the 1984 movie.
body: Michael Douglas revealed in a new excerpt from his memoir One Helluva Ride that he and Kathleen Turner had a secret romantic relationship while filming 1984’s Romancing the Stone, and the actress is responding to his revelation.

“The chemistry I had with Kathleen Turner was so strong, audiences have been certain for years that we were in a relationship together while making the film. We both denied it through Romancing The Stone, Jewel of the Nile, War of the Roses, and even while doing press a few years ago for The Kominsky Method,” he said, noting four projects they’ve worked on together.

“The official story went as follows: Yes, we confessed, we had amazing chemistry. Yes, we were both, as Kathleen said, ‘terrible flirts,’ and yes, we were both tempted, but nothing ever happened between us,” Douglas wrote, per the excerpt. “That was a lie.”

Turner responded to Douglas’ admission on Friday. “Good heavens what a fuss about something 40 years ago!” the actress wrote in a statement shared with People. “I love Michael and I look forward to enjoying the book.”

highlights.title: The Holei Sea Arch, a Centuries-Old Hawaii Wonder, Crumbles Into the Pacific
highlights.summary: A tropical storm was moving through the area when the 90-foot lava rock formation disintegrated, the National Park Service said.
body: For more than half a millennium, one of Hawaii’s most cherished geological marvels, an arch 90 feet high composed of lava rock, withstood a battering from the Pacific and evoked a sense of awe.

But that formation, the Holei Sea Arch at Hawai’i Volcanoes National Park, is now gone from the coastline on the Big Island, having crumbled into the ocean around the same time as a tropical storm brought strong winds and heavy rain to Hawaii in late September, the National Park Service said on Thursday.
A cascade of tributes and vacation photos quickly began pouring in from those who have hiked the park’s rugged coastline over the years, many of them lamenting the landmark’s demise.
The Park Service posted before-and-after photos of the coastline on social media on Thursday night, along with a crying face emoji.

highlights.title: Someone got Doom in an SQL database
highlights.summary: "Rendering Doom in a database is obviously a bad idea," Lukas Vogel writes in a lengthy blog post explaining how exactly he managed to render Doom using an SQL database. OK, that's not entirely accurate.
body: OK, that's not entirely accurate. The SQLDoom project uses a small Python client to handle input and output, drive the game's timing, and display each frame to the screen. Behind that, a series of CedarDB tables tracks the game geometry and state, while about 1,300 lines of SQL queries spread across 89 common table expressions implement the game logic and generate 35 bitmap framebuffers per second.

In this, SQLDoom is a major improvement over Vogel's previous DoomQL project, which last year set out to build "a multiplayer Doom-like shooter entirely in SQL." Unfortunately, that effort ended up with raycasting-based, grayscale ASCII graphics that were more akin to the simplistic 90-degree-angled maps of Wolfenstein 3D. The newer SQLDoom, on the other hand, generates full-color 640x480 frames that look like they could have come from the original Doom executable.

highlights.title: Documenting the tech worker movement
highlights.summary: Writing as a participant and researcher, PhD student JS Tan SM ’22 has co-authored a new book about the rise of tech worker protests and the employer backlash that followed.
body: Despite the “dot-com crash” in 2000, the tech industry remained an attractive career destination for many who believed technology represented the future. The digital age — defined by global connectivity and computers — had firmly taken hold, and over time, the tech industry emerged as a dominant force in the labor market. High-paying jobs for engineers, designers, and professionals across a wide range of fields became increasingly common.
MIT PhD student JS Tan SM ’22 was among those who, upon graduating from Brown University and Rhode Island School of Design in 2015, joined the tech industry.
“A lot of us had this idea that technology, and in particular the technologies related to the internet, had the potential for bringing about a more progressive version of the world,” Tan says.
Google echoed this ethos to its employees with its once-famous motto, “don’t be evil,” as their informal corporate philosophy and code of conduct guideline. They’ve since dropped the tagline.

highlights.title: Pretorius breaks Gayle's T20 record score
highlights.summary: Lhuan-dre Pretorius breaks Chris Gayle's record for the highest score in a men's T20 match with an unbeaten 188 in a domestic fixture in South Africa.
body: The 20-year-old South African's knock off 79 deliveries, including 13 sixes and 15 fours, helped Titans post 267-3 against Knights in the CSA T20 Challenge.
It eclipsed the 175 made by Gayle for Royal Challengers Bangalore (now Bengaluru) against Pune Warriors in the 2013 Indian Premier League.
Pretorius, who has played 17 T20s, three one-dayers and two Tests for South Africa, finished with a strike rate of 237.97.
He made his half-century off 24 balls but only required 16 more balls to get to three figures and then got to 150 off just 58 deliveries.

highlights.title: Fire Emblem Fans Just Cracked Fortune’s Weave’s Biggest Mystery (Maybe)
highlights.summary: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave 's protagonist, Eshmel (or whatever you call them), is a lot like Three Houses ' Byleth. They say little, someone else's soul inhabits their body, and despite ostensibly having no personality, they're the most important person (well, construct) in the empire.
body: This piece contains spoilers for Parts 2 and 3 of Fortune's Weave.

When Fortune's Weave starts, you're literally creating Eshmel. Fortuna and the leader of Kunlun village use ancient space technology to create a Mediator, a theoretically perfect being designed to shepherd the villagers. I have no idea where Mediator souls come from or if they even have souls. (We need DLC with Anatolia's route!) But for Eshmel, Fortuna plucks one out of the aether and says it's fitting for this soul to make amends and restore light to Dagda. The words mean little at the time, and over the course of altering the Flame Lords' fate, you run into a lot of people who really, really need to make amends for one thing or another.

And in the end, Fortune's Weave never directly tells you who Eshmel is, or used to be. They're just the Herald of the Pale Raven, a being of prophecy leading the ruined populace of Dagda in its fight against Balor and the underworld. However, there's a convincing theory circulating around Reddit and GameFAQs about who Eshmel was in their previous life. If you played Cai's route or completed Anna's paralogue, you might've noticed some of these similarities yourself.
points: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave 's protagonist, Eshmel (or whatever you call them), is a lot like Three Houses ' Byleth.
They say little, someone else's soul inhabits their body, and despite ostensibly having no personality, they're the most important person (well, construct) in the empire.

highlights.title: Chicken Scarpariello
highlights.summary: Crispy-skinned chicken thighs, sweet Italian sausage, and roasted potatoes meet a punchy, vinegary pan sauce.
body: Chicken scarpariello (shoemaker’s chicken) brings together crispy-skinned chicken thighs and Italian sausage in a punchy sweet-and-sour pan sauce. This version gets its tang from white wine vinegar and pickled Peppadew peppers, which mingle with onions, fresh bell pepper, garlic, rosemary, and all the savory drippings left behind by the meat.

While some chicken scarpariello recipes cook potatoes right in the pan, we roast fingerlings separately so they stay crisp—perfect for dragging through all that vinegary sauce. Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs are the move here: They brown beautifully, stay juicy as they braise, and add plenty of flavor to the sauce.

Peppadews add sweetness and a mild tang, but hot cherry peppers or pepperoncini work too if you want something sharper or spicier. Serve the scarpariello straight from the skillet for a hearty dinner that lands somewhere between weeknight comfort food and Sunday supper.

highlights.title: Meta open sources code to let you make Muse AI gadgets
highlights.summary: Meta now lets you make your own Muse gadgets that feature the company's new AI agent with code that the company open sourced. The company suggests projects like loading Muse on a color E Ink display to show reminders, adding it to an HDMI stick so you can display Muse on a big screen, or putting…
body: Meta now lets you connect Muse to your own hardware to put on your displays or a Raspberry Pi.

“Muse gadgets are open source devices you build yourself,” Meta says. “Program an off-the-shelf ESP32 board or set up a Raspberry Pi with our SDKs, then connect Muse to your displays, buttons, sensors, actuators, and whatever else you’ve got lying on your workbench.” However, Meta cautions that you should “Proceed at your own risk!”

The company is also giving away a Muse Home Link gadget that it created. With the Muse Home Link, you use community-built skills to have the AI agent “turn on a light, control your TV, send a document to a printer, and more, depending on your setup,” Meta says. It manufactured 5,000 of the gadgets, according to Meta Superintelligence Labs’ Nat Friedman, and you can claim a waitlist spot for the Muse Home Link now ahead of shipping sometime this month.

In a metroidvania, this means a whole lot. End of Abyss is a game about exploration, including lots of backtracking via roundabout paths, so when I'd plan long treks across the world based on a faulty map, it was really frustrating to find out too late that I'd essentially been lied to.

But a patch has fixed that, among other problems, and it presents an uncommon issue for me. My review only went out two days ago. The game only launched yesterday. Now much of my review is already outdated. In this era of live-service games and post-launch updates, it's common for games to change shape over time, but for End of Abyss's patch to fix many of its lesser parts essentially right after the deadline isn't normally how it goes.

highlights.title: These AI Experts Want to Do High-Stakes Research Out in the Open
highlights.summary: Many frontier labs keep their risky research locked away. Trillium Labs wants to show off its work when it comes to self-improvement and model behavior.
body: Some big AI companies seem to think that the best way to keep models from becoming too chaotic or too mischievous is to keep them locked inside of labs. If only a chosen few can access them, the thinking goes, they can do less damage in the real world while researchers try to understand what they’re capable of.

Nathan Lambert and Tom Zick, two industry scientists, believe the opposite. The pair founded a nonprofit, Trillium Labs, that will work on various areas of AI research—including potentially problematic areas like recursive self-improvement (RSI) and agents—in a more transparent way. In practice, this will mean publishing the details of experiments so that outside scientists can study and replicate them.

Lambert says the way frontier AI labs keep their work secret reduces the community’s ability to scrutinize ideas and contribute new approaches. He believes that letting outside experts see how models are built and tuned could be crucial to mitigating risks.

The conductors who oversee the recording of the movie scores are portrayed as hyper-demanding corporate perfectionists. (One of them, a prima donna played by Thomas Kretschmann, makes it feel like you’re seeing Klaus Kinski going to work for Skydance.) And from the film’s opening scene, which immerses us in the lingo of rehearsal, which is a mixture of old-school classical Euro directives (“pianissimo”) and Hollywood jargon (“new ink”), we’re right there in the cavernous recording studio, feeling the heat and the nuance.

Alex, after the debacle of his break-up with Wilde’s clingy diva in Chicago, returns to Los Angeles, where he grew up. He can get session work there, and does. He still seems mellow, but he’s bestirred by a pet obsession: listening to the original avant-pop compositions posted online by Viviana ( Alexa Swinton ), a 15-year-old girl who has become a local celebrity. It turns out that he’s got a connection to her; she’s Nadia’s daughter. But why is he so interested? He’s just got…a feeling.

highlights.title: Patient-zero drill put health facilities to the test—40% of them failed
highlights.summary: COVID-19 made the weaknesses in our pandemic preparedness at national and global levels painfully clear. But a new study highlights that even at the first, local steps of an outbreak with pandemic-potential, we are worryingly underprepared.
body: Health officials in New York set up a regional test of healthcare facilities to identify and respond to a patient with a mystery infection that could pose a pandemic-level threat. But things didn’t go well. Overall, responses were slow, appropriate use of personal protective equipment was spotty, and only 60 percent of facilities passed the basics of the test—an overall failing grade.

“These drills identified needs for health care workers and health care facility staff member training to achieve earlier identification, masking, and isolation of potentially infectious febrile patients,” the officials wrote in the study, which was published in the Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report.

To pass the test, a healthcare facility needed to mask the patient and put them in an isolation room. Ideally, the masking would occur within a minute or less of the patient walking in, and isolation would occur in 10 minutes or less. For this drill, both masking and isolation were enough to pass, regardless of timing.

highlights.title: Redefining enterprise intelligence with autonomous AI
highlights.summary: Enterprise AI is no longer a future ambition. It is in full operational flight. Model capabilities are advancing faster than most organizations can absorb, while the cost of performance continues to fall. Globally, AI investment is set to reach $2.5 trillion in 2026, up 44% from the previous year.
body: For many enterprises, this investment has produced fragmentation. Intelligence can accumulate in silos so that sales agents are unaware of open support tickets, for instance, or marketing systems are personalizing content without visibility into what finance already knows about a customer. Each function may perform well in isolation, but the enterprise as a whole learns little and has less information to act upon.

The shift from AI as a tool to AI as an operating model—what we call the “agentic shift” in this report—demands something more fundamental than better models or faster infrastructure. It requires connecting people, processes, and data in real time, along with the governance and control to act on that intelligence reliably.

This means rethinking both architecture and operating models simultaneously. First, rebuilding data infrastructure for accessibility rather than volume. Second, replacing fixed tech stacks with composable architectures that can evolve as models and tools change. And, lastly, resolving questions of AI sovereignty, including where intelligence runs, who controls it, and how it operates across organizational and jurisdictional boundaries.
points: Enterprise AI is no longer a future ambition.
Model capabilities are advancing faster than most organizations can absorb, while the cost of performance continues to fall.

For many enterprises, this investment has produced fragmentation.

highlights.title: They’re delicious, popular and versatile – but how healthy are berries?
highlights.summary: Experts say that if you’re eating any berry – strawberries, blackberries, currants, raspberries, blueberries – you are benefiting. Sprinkled on top of yoghurt, blended into smoothies or baked into crumbles, berries are among Americans’ favorite fruits.
body: Luckily, berries are as healthy as they are delicious and versatile: low in calories, full of vitamins and antioxidants, and a good source of fiber. Research shows that, depending on the type, berries support cardiovascular health, may boost gut health and fight inflammation and show promise as part of a “healthy dietary strategy for diabetes prevention and management”, to quote researchers. Meta-analyses also link compounds in berries with improved cognitive health.
“Berries’ high polyphenol content is what we think makes them so protective” when it comes to mental processes such as memory and attention, said Maggie Moon, a registered dietitian.

Polyphenols are a broad category of plant compounds; in berries, the most active and proportionally meaningful of them are anthocyanins, which also give many berries their blue, purple and red pigments.

Researchers are investigating whether berry polyphenols and the metabolites produced when gut microbes process them may influence inflammation and blood-vessel function. Because the brain depends on an extensive blood supply, better vascular function is one plausible route by which berries could support cognition.

Luckily, berries are as healthy as they are delicious and versatile: low in calories, full of vitamins and antioxidants, and a good source of fiber.
“Berries’ high polyphenol content is what we think makes them so protective” when it comes to mental processes such as memory and attention, said Maggie Moon, a registered dietitian.
